'''Cog Hive Seven''' was a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Prison/Legends|prison]] in the [[Tharin sector/Legends|Tharin sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] that was used as a [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] [[Death/Legends|death]] match [[Gambling/Legends|gambling]] operation by its owners in the waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].

The space station, which had a fluid architecture capable of highly complex levels of reconfiguration, was constructed around the year [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]] based on an algorithm written by [[Dakarai Blirr]] and funded by the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]]. Dakarai's sister [[Sadiki Blirr|Sadiki]] became [[Warden/Legends|Warden]] of Cog Hive Seven after its rushed completion. The Blirr siblings would win millions of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] on every twice-daily death match, and their algorithm had a 100% success rate, which brought them into conflict with the [[Galactic Gaming Commission]].<ref name="Lock" />

The extremely reclusive weapons manufacturer and dealer [[Iram Radique]] used Cog Hive Seven as his base of operations under the nose of Warden Blirr. [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] had masterminded an assassination plot against his own [[Sith Master/Legends|dark master]] which involved the prison, and Sidious tasked his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] with [[Mission to Cog Hive Seven|infiltrating]] the prison and the structured criminal empire operating within it. While imprisoned in Cog Hive Seven with the assumed under-cover name "Jagganath", Maul participated in four of the prison's ongoing gladiatorial death matches of inmates against the inmates.<ref name="Lock" />

==Behind the scenes==
Cog Hive Seven first appeared in "[[The Syrox Redemption]]," a short story published in [[Star Wars Insider 146|''Star Wars Insider'' 146]] and authored by [[Joe Schreiber]]. The story introduces elements of the<ref name="Syrox Redemption">{{InsiderCite|146|The Syrox Redemption}}</ref> [[2014]] novel ''[[Maul: Lockdown]]'', which was also written by Schreiber and features Cog Hive Seven as its main setting.<ref name="Lock" />
